headline: Spatial and single-cell methods quantify gene, morphology and context relationships at finer resolution
label: Spatial Quantification And Identifiability
summary: New tools quantify sub-gene, spatial and trajectory-level structure in single-cell and spatial data, with explicit statistical frameworks and efficiency gains.
synthesis: The common thread is quantification that specifies the unit of inference, whether sub-gene probe counts, gene-wise histology effects, spatial gene relationships or cellular neighborhoods. simpleaf is extended to quantify probe-based multiplexed data at sub-gene resolution with lower runtime and memory than cyto and Cell Ranger. MorphoANOVA uses nested spatially varying coefficient models and sequential ANOVA to link H&E morphology to expression. GeneSPOT applies gene-centric optimal transport to measure how spatial gene relationships reorganize across conditions and time, while Sphinx models adaptive neighborhoods in spatial proteomics. CellChat Hotspot adds gene-set enrichment and filtering to communication inference, with spatial transcriptomics validation. SCALEMAP addresses scalable diagonal integration of unpaired multi-omics. MIST and BEHAV3D-Explorer extend context-aware phenotyping to single-molecule and 3D live imaging.
